newsitem.title: USA: Ruling imminent in Simpson child-custody battle.
newsitem.headline: Ruling imminent in Simpson child-custody battle.

text.p: An attorney attacked the credibility of a key defence witness at the O.J. Simpson civil trial on Friday as both sides awaited a family court judge's ruling in the former football star's child custody battle.

Sources involved in the civil case said it appeared increasingly unlikely there would be enough time for Simpson to take the witness stand as planned on Friday before the trial goes into a two-week holiday recess.

Simpson was absent from the Santa Monica courtroom for the morning session and was reportedly huddling with his legal advisers about a ruling expected on Friday afternoon in his battle for custody of the two children he had with Nicole Brown Simpson.
Louis and Juditha Brown have been caring for their grandchildren, 11-year-old Sydney and 8-year-old Justin, since just after their daughter's 1994 murder.

Simpson, who was acquitted in October 1995 in the killings of his ex-wife and her friend Ronald Goldman, is now on trial in civil court facing a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.
Simpson turned over temporary guardianship of the children to their maternal grandparents after his June 17, 1994, arrest, but now he wants them back.
At the civil trial, amateur photo analyst Robert Groden returned for a second day of testimony, only to come under bruising cross-examination by plaintiffs' attorney Peter Gelblum.
Groden testified on Wednesday that a 1993 photograph of Simpson apparently wearing the same kind of expensive designer shoes worn by the killer was most likely a fake.

But Gelblum lashed out at Groden on Friday, pointing out he had no formal training or professional credentials in photographic analysis and suggesting he was a conspiracy buff who was testifying for the money.

Groden, a Dallas photo technician who has spent years analysing pictures of the John F. Kennedy assassination, acknowledged he was being paid $8,000 by Simpson's defence team. Asked to describe how important his Kennedy assassination studies were to him, Groden said: "It's my life's work."

Groden, who was called by Simpson's attorneys, testified on Wednesday there was a "high likelihood of forgery" in the 1993 photo, which was taken by a freelance photographer at a pro football game in Buffalo, New York, and was later published in the National Enquirer.

The photo, which was introduced earlier by the plaintiffs, shows Simpson wearing the same kind of Italian-made Bruno Magli shoes that left bloody shoeprints near the bodies of Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman. In testimony last month Simpson denied he ever owned shoes like those in the photo.

Under questioning by Simpson attorney Dan Leonard, Groden testified on Wednesday that his analysis of the photo showed problems with colour balance and tone, alignment of the negative on a film strip and evidence of re-touching.

Simpson, who faced harsh interrogation from opposing attorneys last month, was on the official witness list to make his second appearance on Friday, this time under gentler questioning by his own lawyers.

But it appeared the lengthy questioning of Groden and the upcoming testimony by chemist Fredric Rieders would probably consume the entire court session. The trial will then be in recess for the Christmas and New Year's holidays until Jan. 6.
